_comment: Copy this file to hydra_bench.config.json (git-ignored) and replace every placeholder. Use absolute paths with forward slashes. Any key can instead be given as an environment variable HYDRA_BENCH_<KEY> (dots become underscores, e.g. HYDRA_BENCH_MODELS_MF6; lists as JSON text). A missing key stops the script and names it. No engine or model is distributed with this repository.
_comment_work_root: Folder where the benchmark makes copies of the models and writes results.json, baseline.json, ... Keep it OUTSIDE every model folder; the original models are never modified.
_comment_node_path: Node.js executable used to run bench/tool_report.js. A full path, or just node if it is on PATH.
_comment_models: Folder of one WORKING model per engine: the folder that holds the model input files (for SWAT+ the TxtInOut folder). Faults are injected into copies of these.
_comment_executables: The engine executable that runs each model above. You supply them; none is distributed. It is copied into every work folder and run there. For mf6, libmf6.dll next to mf6.exe is copied as well.
_comment_audit_targets: Model folders for tests/audit_fp.js (false-positive audit) and tests/scan_rows.js. set = label for the table; status = published | reference to treat a folder as working without a success.fin marker; expand_prefix = use every sub-folder of dir whose name starts with it. Absent folders are skipped.
_comment_rules_real_folders: tests/run_rules_node.js: model folders that RAN; the rules must raise no ERROR on them. With no configuration at all these cases are skipped (the synthetic cases still run); with a configuration the key is required.
_comment_rules_true_positive_folders: tests/run_rules_node.js: folders where an ERROR whose title matches the regular expression pattern is expected (a model that ran but has a real defect).

rules_true_positive_folders.name: a model with a known defect

_comment_fixture_sources: tests/make_fixtures.py: folders whose first lines are stored in tests/fixtures.js (git-ignored). depth = how many folder levels to read.
